text:
[LSTR.3.1] String equality is codepoint-by-codepoint. Two
strings are equal iff they have the same length and matching
codepoints at every position. No normalisation is applied; the
NFC and NFD forms of the same grapheme cluster are not equal: `café` spelled
with U+00E9 is not equal to `café` spelled with U+0065 U+0301.

idris.name: iret_7_5__cmp_str
idris.note: A String compared with a String: `==` and `!=` by this clause's equality, the orderings by [LSTR.3.2]'s order; a `null` right operand propagates ([LNUL.4.1]); anything else is ill-typed, a trap.

idris.name: iret_7_5__str_order
idris.note: The six comparisons on two texts: `==` and `!=` the equality codepoint by codepoint, `<` and `>` [LSTR.3.2]'s order, `<=` and `>=` the order or the equality.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__cp_cmp_eq
idris.note: Two codepoints the structural comparison calls EQ are one codepoint.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__eq
idris.note: Equality of two texts: the same length and the same codepoint at every position, the structural codepoint comparison deciding each; no normalisation.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__eq_at
idris.note: One step of the equality: equal heads leave it to the tails, any other pair decides false.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__eq_refl
idris.note: Every text equals itself, by induction on the text.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__eq_sound
idris.note: Two texts the test calls equal are one text, for every pair: the same length and matching codepoints at every position, the clause's iff read from the test's side.

idris.name: lstr_3_1__nfc_is_not_nfd
idris.note: The clause's example, executed: `café` with U+00E9 and `café` with U+0065 U+0301 are not equal.

idris.name: lstr_3_2__lt_total
idris.note: Two texts this clause calls unequal are ordered one way or the other by [LSTR.3.2]'s order: equality and order together are total on texts.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2__corr_is
idris.note: A read correlation is the sweep's under LSTR.3.1's codepoint equality; a fact that reads none never matches.
